answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity expensive rather than free: every agent must post a bond locked on-ledger, and payment routing weights each agent by a slowly-decaying record of independent counterparties. Padding the population with a sonnet of cloned wallets buys nothing, because fresh accounts share no distinct payers and their bonds sit in escrow. Attackers must therefore fund and lock real capital per synthetic identity, a sunk cost that a reef of fake peers can never recover, while the honest tundra of bonded agents stays profitable.
